newsitem.title: UK: Most U.S. stocks in soft in London, but oil firms.
newsitem.headline: Most U.S. stocks in soft in London, but oil firms.

text.p: Most U.S. stocks were weaker in London on Monday amid fears the Federal Reserve will tighten credit policy when policymakers meet tomorrow, but the oil sector continued to firm, traders said.
On thin volume, most shares sank, and traders here were calling the Dow 15 to 20 points lower at the open.

The December S&P 500 futures contract was 2.50 points lower at 689.40 on Globex at 1032 GMT, while the December 30-year Treasury bond futures contract, which has already factored in higher interest rates, was down 6/32 at 107-19/32.
"Bonds and equities have diverged a bit. Bonds have priced in a 25 basis point increase (in the fed funds rate), but stocks were driven last week by a huge influx in mutual funds," said one trader.
Worries about the health of Russian leader Boris Yeltsin also dimmed the tone for U.S. shares, traders said.
Bucking the weaker trend were oil shares, up on concerns about supply disruptions, expectations that demand will outstrip supplies, and on a broker recommendations, traders said.
Shares in Atlantic Richfield were up $1/4 to $126 in London. Shares in Mobile and Texaco were up $1/4 and $1/8 to $119-7/8 and $95-3/8, respectively.

In other trading, shares in Coca Cola fell $1/2 to $50-5/8 in London after the drink maker told analysts that its global volume in the third quarter will rise by a weaker-than-expected six to seven percent.

Shares in Pepsico were off $1/8 to $30, but the stock was to some extent underpinned by a report in U.S. financial paper Barron's that discussed at the possibility of a spinoff of Pepsico's restaurants unit, one trader said.
U.S. technology shares also weakened. Shares in Intel slipped $1/8 to $97-1/4 despite a favourable article in Barrons, traders noted.
